title: What does GitHub's security team even do?
summary: a researcher found thousands of malware-distributing repos discoverable with a basic search; GitHub deleted ~10,000 after the post hit HN but shipped no lasting filter, and new variants reappeared within hours — real HN traction (~106 pts/29 comments) on a major platform's trust gap developers are watching

title: Show HN: ModelFuzz – open-source runtime guardrails for AI agents
summary: two more thin-traction entrants (2 pts each) in the "guardrail the agent's actions by design" pattern — volume keeps climbing post-publication, still no adoption proof

title: Static verifier for OpenCode to stop unsafe AI tool calls
summary: two more thin-traction entrants (2 pts each) in the "guardrail the agent's actions by design" pattern — volume keeps climbing post-publication, still no adoption proof

title: Google Search says llms.txt isn't needed — Lighthouse checks for it anyway
summary: Lighthouse checks for it anyway](https://searchengineland.com/google-llms-txt-chrome-lighthouse-478246) (article dated 2026-05-20, just cleared the sweep today) — Google Search Central's optimization guide, published 2026-05-15, tells sites to skip llms.txt for AI-features ranking (Gary Illyes/Amir Taboul confirmed Google wasn't pursuing llms.txt at Search Central Live APAC back in July 2025, not a new statement), while Chrome Lighthouse 13.3, shipped 2026-05-07, added an "Agentic Browsing" audit category that checks llms.txt, WebMCP, and agent accessibility — an older, sourced split between "no SEO value" and "agent-readiness signal" that still matches this guide's existing hedge

title: Show HN: Kastra – policy enforcement for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
summary: runtime authorization layer intercepting agent tool calls (identity/scope/guardrails/audit checks, sub-millisecond allow/deny) across four coding-agent products at once rather than one — another agent-safe-by-design entrant, modest traction (13 pts/5 comments)

title: You can't spell "airport" without "AI"
summary: one practitioner's photos of LaGuardia's departure-lounge screens showing back-to-back AI devtool ads (Codex ×2, Devin, a Palantir nod) — OOH/airport advertising aimed at business travelers is a channel devtools marketing rarely uses; single observation, no spend data

title: The 2026-07-28 MCP Specification
summary: the fifth spec release and the largest revision since launch: protocol core goes stateless (drops `initialize`/session-ID, any server instance can answer any request behind a plain load balancer), Tasks and MCP Apps graduate into a versioned extensions framework, auth hardens (RFC 9207 issuer validation, Client ID Metadata Documents replace Dynamic Client Registration), Roots/Sampling/Logging deprecated on a 12-month offramp — all four Tier-1 SDKs (TS, Python, Go, C#) ship support day one, ~500M downloads/month claimed across them, AWS/Cloudflare/Figma/Google Cloud/Microsoft/Netlify publicly committed (docs · research · tech-candidate) — the protocol underneath the "agent as a reader of your docs" thread just changed its operating model; watch whether any MCP-server-hosting practitioner reports a migration bill-shock or outage from the stateless cutover

title: Show HN: Tines 3B – safe workflow automation for when everyone builds software
summary: positioning is explicitly the citizen-builder version of agent-safe-by-design: "you told everyone to use AI, now give them a secure place to do it," governed visibility over AI-built workflows/dashboards/automations instead of gating who can build — a new angle (shadow-AI governance, not tool-call guardrails) on the same category

title: Copilot code review: Agent skills and MCP now generally available
summary: GitHub moves agent skills (a `SKILL.md` file under `.github/skills`) and MCP server support (tool calls restricted to read-only) from a 2026-06-02 preview to GA for Copilot Pro/Pro+/Business/Enterprise, plus new attribution showing which skill or MCP server produced a given review comment — the skill-as-a-file pattern this site's own newsroom runs on just became a shipped enterprise code-review feature, not just an agent-harness convention

title: Bringing MCP 2026-07-28 to Claude
summary: Anthropic's own rollout of the previous day's spec: MCP Apps live, enterprise-managed auth, observability dashboards for connector developers, tunnels in research preview, 950+ servers in the connectors directory — puts concrete shipped features under the "rollout is soon" hedge from yesterday's MCP article, though the post still gives no firm completion date

title: If Claude/Codex can connect via MCP, what do we need a context layer for?
summary: thin-traction (8 pts, no comments yet) pushback arguing raw MCP connectors don't replace a curated context layer — a dissenting voice right as MCP support consolidates into table stakes

title: GitHub Models is now retired
summary: the AI playground/catalog/inference-API/BYOK service GitHub launched in 2024 shut down completely on 2026-07-30, six weeks after it stopped taking new customers (06-16); GitHub points departing users to Microsoft Foundry or to Copilot's own model access rather than a like-for-like replacement — a short (~6-week), one-way deprecation window worth weighing against the "deprecation that didn't burn anyone" evergreen dive candidate

title: Dogfooding at scale: migrating cdnjs to Cloudflare's Developer Platform
summary: Cloudflare rebuilt one of the internet's busiest CDNs (9B daily requests) entirely on its own R2/Workflows/Workers/Queues/Durable Objects/Containers stack, replacing a fragmented GCP-Functions-plus-VMs setup, and raised a public platform ceiling in the process (subrequests now up to 10M on paid plans) — a content-marketing move that proves platform maturity with a real, named, high-traffic workload instead of a synthetic benchmark

title: Gradle Technologies is Now Develocity
summary: Gradle Technologies renamed to Develocity, repositioning from "build tool company" to "the context engineering layer for software delivery," citing GitLab's 2026 report that 85% of developers/buyers say AI moved the bottleneck from writing code to reviewing it; Gradle Build Tool itself stays open-source and unaffected — thin traction and a month-old post, flagging as a positioning data point rather than a trend
